chunks: [Description of Allāh] Praise be to Allāh whom refusal to give away and stinginess do not make rich,
and Whom munificence and generosity do not make poor, although everyone who gives away loses (to that extent) except He,
and every miser is blamed for his niggardliness.
He obliges through beneficial bounties and plentiful gifts and grants.
The whole creation is His dependents (in sustenance) [2]. He has guaranteed their livelihood and ordained their sustenance.
He has prepared the way for those who turn to Him and those who seek what is with Him.
He is as generous about what He is asked as He is about that for which He is not asked.
ai.seo_question: How is Allāh's generosity different from human generosity according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage, part of the 'Al-Ashbaah' chapter detailing the creation of the universe, establishes a metaphysical distinction between the Creator and the created by highlighting Allah's infinite generosity. In Shia theological discourse, this underscores the concept of *al-Manan* (The Bestower of Favors), affirming that divine giving does not entail depletion (*nقص*), contrasting with the finite nature of created beings. It serves as a foundational argument for Allah's self-sufficiency (*Al-Ghani*) and the gratuitous nature of His blessings, which exceed mere transactional reciprocity.
